Pi Health, Inc. submits the attached formal response to the US Food and Drug Administration's Request for Information on the AI-Enabled Optimization of Early-Phase Clinical Trials Pilot Program (Docket No. FDA-2026-N-4390).

Pi Health is an AI-native clinical trial platform company headquartered in Cambridge, MA, and the developer of FICS (Front-End Interoperable Capture Software), a unified intelligent platform managing the full clinical trial lifecycle on a single governed data layer.

Our response provides substantive recommendations on pilot program design, participant selection criteria, collaboration models, evaluation metrics, and AI trustworthiness standards aligned with the NIST AI RMF. Key positions include: (1) the pilot's success depends on data integrity, not only data connectivity; (2) participant selection should favor sponsor-agnostic, software-native platforms to ensure generalizability across the broader biopharmaceutical ecosystem; and (3) evaluation metrics must encompass AI trustworthiness and GxP compliance, not only trial speed.

Respectfully submitted,

Bobby Reddy, MD
President, CEO & Co-Founder, Pi Health, Inc.

Todd Palmby, PhD
Chief Scientific Officer and Head of Regulatory Affairs, Pi Health, Inc.
